def-qft-regular-polynomial-functional-al:
## Definition

Let $d\ge1$, $X=\mathbb R^d$, and $n\ge1$. Write
$\mathcal D(X^n)=C_c^\infty(X^n;\mathbb C)$ for the complex test-function
space of smooth compactly supported functions
([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]), with its LF topology
([[def-test-function-topology]]). The convergence criterion used below is
that convergent test sequences have one common compact support and converge
uniformly with every derivative
([[thm-sequential-convergence-in-test-function-space]]). Here $C^\infty$
means every coordinate derivative exists and is continuous
([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]). All integrals are
compact Riemann integrals: each integrand is continuous with compact support,
so restrict it to a compact rectangle and apply
[[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]. Let
$\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sym}}(X^n)$ be the subspace of kernels invariant under
every permutation of their $n$ $X$-variables. Fields are real smooth
configurations $\phi\in C^\infty(X;\mathbb R)$. For an integer $N\ge0$
and a finite family
$f_0\in\mathbb C$, $f_n\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sym}}(X^n)$ for
$1\le n\le N$, define
$$ F_f(\phi)=f_0+\sum_{n=1}^{N}\int_{X^n}f_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\prod_{j=1}^{n}\phi(x_j)\,dx_1\cdots dx_n. $$
The pairing is complex-bilinear, with no conjugation on the kernel or field.
An element of $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(X)$ is this finite symmetric
coefficient family, evaluated on fields by $F_f$. Pointwise sums, scalar
multiples, and products again have finite symmetric compactly supported
coefficient families: for products, expand the two finite sums and
symmetrize each tensor product $f_m\otimes g_n$. Thus these elements form
an algebra; the product-integral identity follows from Riemann Fubini on a
rectangle containing the compact supports
([[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]]).

For $k=0$, set $F_f^{(0)}(\phi)=F_f(\phi)$. For $1\le k\le N$,
the $k$-th functional derivative kernel assigned to this coefficient
family is
$$ F_f^{(k)}(\phi)(x_1,\ldots,x_k)=\sum_{n=k}^{N}\frac{n!}{(n-k)!}\int_{X^{n-k}}f_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\prod_{j=k+1}^{n}\phi(x_j)\,dx_{k+1}\cdots dx_n. $$
For $k>N$ it is zero. Each displayed kernel is smooth, symmetric and compactly supported in its $k$ remaining variables: compactness follows by projection of the finite union of coefficient-kernel supports, and derivatives pass through the finite-compact integrals by [[thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign-on-a-compact-rectangle]].
In the term $n=k$, the empty integral and empty product mean simply
$f_k(x_1,\ldots,x_k)$.

The scope is exactly smooth compact coefficient kernels. A local functional
whose higher derivative kernels are distributions on a thin diagonal is not
included merely because its field expression is polynomial.
thm-qft-diagonal-delta-distribution:
## Statement

Let $X=\mathbb R^4$ and let $\Delta_X=\{(x,y)\in X\times X:x=y\}$.
For $\Psi\in\mathcal D(X\times X)$, define
$$ \langle\delta_{\Delta_X},\Psi\rangle =\int_X\Psi(x,x)\,d^4x. $$
Then $\delta_{\Delta_X}\in\mathcal D'(X\times X)$ is a continuous
complex-linear distribution with support exactly $\Delta_X$, and it is
symmetric under exchanging $x$ and $y$. No nonzero smooth function on
$X\times X$ is supported on $\Delta_X$.
thm-qft-bounded-regulator-dyson-factoriz:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal H$ be a complex Hilbert space
([[def-hilbert-space]]), $I=[a,b]$ with $a\le b$,
and $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ a strongly continuous family of
self-adjoint bounded operators (self-adjoint means $V(t)=V(t)^*$, using the
Hilbert adjoint of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]) with
$M:=\sup_{t\in I}\|V(t)\|<\infty$. Strong continuity means that
$t\mapsto V(t)\psi$ is norm-continuous for every $\psi\in\mathcal H$.
Define $U_0(t,s)=I_{\mathcal H}$ and recursively
$$ U_{n+1}(t,s)\psi=-i\int_s^t V(r)U_n(r,s)\psi\,dr,\qquad a\le s,t\le b, $$
where the integral is the vector-valued Riemann integral and is oriented when
$t<s$. Then
$$ \|U_0(t,s)\|\le1,\qquad \|U_n(t,s)\|\le \frac{M^n|t-s|^n}{n!}\quad(n\ge1). $$
For every complex $z$, $U_z(t,s)=\sum_{n\ge0}z^nU_n(t,s)$ converges in
operator norm, uniformly on $I^2$, and is the unique strongly continuous
solution of
$$ U_z(t,s)=I_{\mathcal H}-iz\int_s^t V(r)U_z(r,s)\,dr . $$
For real $z$, $U_z(t,s)$ is unitary and obeys
$U_z(t,r)U_z(r,s)=U_z(t,s)$. If $V_2$ vanishes outside $[a,c]$ and
$V_1$ vanishes outside $[d,b]$, where $c<d$, then
$$ U_z^{V_1+V_2}(b,a)=U_z^{V_1}(b,a)U_z^{V_2}(b,a), $$
with the later-time factor on the left, provided $a\le c<d\le b$. This
identity also holds
coefficientwise as a formal power series in $z$.
lem-qft-tensor-test-function-density:
## Statement

Let $d,n\ge1$, $X=\mathbb R^d$, and give
$\mathcal D(X^n)=C_c^\infty(X^n;\mathbb C)$ its LF test-function topology.
The finite linear span of elementary product tests
$$ (x_1,\ldots,x_n)\longmapsto\prod_{j=1}^{n}g_j(x_j),\qquad g_j\in\mathcal D(X), $$
is dense. More precisely, for each $\Phi\in\mathcal D(X^n)$, there is a
sequence of such finite sums whose supports lie in one fixed compact product
and whose derivatives of every multi-index converge uniformly to those of
$\Phi$. Symmetrized finite sums are dense in
$\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sym}}(X^n)$. Consequently the symmetric-kernel
representation in [[def-qft-regular-polynomial-functional-algebra]] is
unique: if a finite symmetric-kernel polynomial vanishes on every real smooth
field, every coefficient kernel vanishes.
thm-qft-regular-wick-star-associativity:
## Statement

Let $X=\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, and let $W\in\mathcal D'(X\times X)$ be
any continuous complex bidistribution. For a real formal parameter $\eta$
and $F,G\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(X)$, define
$$ F\star_W G=\sum_{k\ge0}\frac{\eta^k}{k!}\left\langle W^{\otimes k},F^{(k)}(\phi)\otimes G^{(k)}(\phi)\right\rangle . $$
The pairing is over $k$ independent pairs of variables; $W^{\otimes k}$
is formed by iterated distributional tensor products, not by multiplying
distributions at coincident points. The sum is finite because the inputs are
polynomial. It defines an element of
$\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(X)[\eta]$, and $\star_W$ is associative.
If $W$ is Hermitian in the sense
$\overline{\langle W,\overline g\otimes\overline f\rangle}
=\langle W,f\otimes g\rangle$, then
$(F\star_W G)^*=G^*\star_W F^*$, where $F^*(\phi)=\overline{F(\phi)}$.
For $\ell_f(\phi)=\int_X f(x)\phi(x)\,dx$,
$$ [\ell_f,\ell_g]_{\star_W}=\eta\bigl(W(f,g)-W(g,f)\bigr), \qquad W(f,g):=\langle W,f\otimes g\rangle . $$
lem-qft-regular-normal-order-isomorphism:
## Statement

Let $W\in\mathcal D'(X\times X)$, $X=\mathbb R^d$, and let
$K\in\mathcal D'(X\times X)$ be symmetric under interchange of its
variables. Define
$$ \Gamma_KF(\phi)=\langle K,F^{(2)}(\phi)\rangle,\qquad \alpha_K=\exp\!\left(\frac{\eta}{2}\Gamma_K\right) =\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{(\eta/2)^j}{j!}\Gamma_K^j $$
on $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(X)[\eta]$. Each sum is finite on each
polynomial because $\Gamma_K$ lowers degree by two. Then $\alpha_K$ is
invertible with inverse $\alpha_{-K}$, and
$$ \alpha_K(F\star_W G)=\alpha_K(F)\star_{W+K}\alpha_K(G) $$
for all regular polynomial functionals $F,G$. Thus the change from $W$
to $W+K$ is an exact algebra isomorphism on this regular class.
def-qft-regular-formal-time-ordering:
## Definition

Fix $\mu\ge0$ and the $(-+++)$, shell, Fourier, and coordinate conventions
of [[lem-qft-free-time-ordered-kernel]]. That current supplier states that
its relative-coordinate tempered distribution $H_\mu$ is symmetric, agrees
with the ordered Wightman kernels on strictly ordered time supports and on
spacelike-separated supports, and has no prefactor $i$ in its definition.
Its current carrier is a draft with a supplied conditional proof; the formula
below uses that exact interface.

For open $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ is the space
of smooth compactly supported complex tests with the LF topology, and
$\mathcal D'(\Omega)$ is its continuous complex-linear dual, paired
bilinearly with no conjugation
([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[def-test-function-topology]],
[[def-distribution]]). Schwartz space consists of smooth functions with all
polynomially weighted derivatives bounded; $\mathcal S'$ is its continuous
complex-linear dual with bilinear pairing
([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]],
[[def-schwartz-topology-and-convergence]], [[def-tempered-distribution]]).

For any relative-coordinate distribution $K\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^4)$,
define its translation-invariant two-point bidistribution
$\widetilde K\in\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^4\times\mathbb R^4)$ by
$$ \langle\widetilde K,\Psi\rangle =\left\langle K,\ z\longmapsto\int_{\mathbb R^4}\Psi(y+z,y)\,dy\right\rangle, \qquad \Psi\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^4\times\mathbb R^4). $$
The inner function is a test function: its support lies in the difference
of the two compact coordinate projections of $\operatorname{supp}\Psi$;
each derivative in $z$ is the Riemann integral of the corresponding
first-variable derivative of $\Psi$ over a compact rectangle containing
the fixed compact second-variable projection
([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]).
On each fixed compact support space, every output derivative seminorm is
bounded by the volume of a compact rectangle containing the second-variable
projection times the corresponding source derivative seminorm. The support
of the output lies in the compact difference of the two projections. Thus
this map is continuous on each fixed-support test space, and hence on the LF
test topology [[def-test-function-topology]].
Thus the displayed formula defines a distribution without multiplying
singular distributions. Write $\mathsf H_\mu=\widetilde H_\mu$.

For $F\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(\mathbb R^4)$, define its support as the
finite union of the coordinate projections of the supports of its nonconstant
symmetric coefficient kernels. This is a compact set and is presentation
independent by [[lem-qft-tensor-test-function-density]]. For compact
$A,B\subset\mathbb R^4$, write $A\succcurlyeq_{\mathrm{out}} B$ when
$$ x-y\notin C_-:=\{(t,\mathbf x)\in\mathbb R^4:t\le-|\mathbf x|\} \quad\text{for every }x\in A,\ y\in B. $$
This means the first support has no point in the closed causal past of the
second, using the supplier's fixed inertial chart.

For $n\ge2$ and $1\le i<j\le n$, let $D_{\mathsf H}^{ij}$ contract one
functional derivative in slots $i,j$ against $\mathsf H_\mu$, pairing
independent variables. Define
$$ T_n^H(F_1,\ldots,F_n)(\phi) =\left.m_n\exp\!\left(\eta\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}D_{\mathsf H}^{ij}\right) \prod_{i=1}^nF_i(\phi_i)\right|_{\phi_1=\cdots=\phi_n=\phi}, \qquad T_0^H=1,\quad T_1^H(F)=F. $$
Here $m_n$ multiplies the remaining factors and then substitutes the same
field $\phi$ in every slot; on coefficient kernels it symmetrizes their
finite tensor products. The parameter $\eta$ is formal and fixed by
complex conjugation. Each contraction removes two polynomial degrees, so the
exponential is a finite sum on polynomial inputs. The dependencies
[[thm-tensor-product-distributions-and-iterated-pairings]] and
[[lem-distribution-pairing-with-smooth-parameter-families]] make every
contraction well defined and leave smooth compact kernels in the uncontracted
variables; no diagonal product occurs. Symmetry of $\mathsf H_\mu$ makes
$T_n^H$ symmetric in its inputs.

For a regular compactly supported interaction $V$ and formal coupling $z$,
define
$$ S_z^H(V)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(iz/\eta)^n}{n!}\,T_n^H(V,\ldots,V) \quad\text{with coefficients in }\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(\mathbb R^4)[\eta,\eta^{-1}]. $$
This is a coefficientwise formal series; the definition asserts no
convergence in $z$, no time-ordered product for singular local functionals,
and no continuum interacting field.
thm-qft-regular-formal-causal-factorizat:
## Statement

Assume the current scalar suppliers
[[lem-qft-free-time-ordered-kernel]],
[[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]], and
[[lem-qft-scalar-causal-commutator]] at exactly their displayed draft
interfaces. Let $W_\mu$ be the relative-coordinate scalar Wightman
distribution from the smeared-field supplier, and let $H_\mu$ be the
time-ordered relative-coordinate distribution from the time-ordered-kernel
supplier. Form their translation-invariant bidistributions by the construction
in [[def-qft-regular-formal-time-ordering]].

Let $V,U\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(\mathbb R^4)$ have compact supports
$A,B$, respectively. If $A\succcurlyeq_{\mathrm{out}}B$, as defined in
[[def-qft-regular-formal-time-ordering]], then
$$ S_z^H(V+U)=S_z^H(V)\star_{W_\mu}S_z^H(U) $$
coefficientwise in $z$. If every difference $x-y$, $x\in A$,
$y\in B$, is spacelike, then $F\star_{W_\mu}G=G\star_{W_\mu}F$ for
regular $F,G$ supported in $A,B$; the corresponding formal series commute
coefficientwise. These are formal identities for regular functionals only.
They assert neither convergence in the coupling nor a local Wick-product or
continuum-interaction construction.
